prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core pitch
- Stay with the Conservative plan to secure the economy, borders, energy and defence; reward work; support families; and strengthen communities. Contrast drawn with Labour on tax, spending, immigration and defence.

Economy and tax
- Fiscal rules maintained; borrowing and debt to fall on target.
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
- “Triple Lock Plus” for pensioners: state pension and a new age‑related personal allowance both rise by the highest of earnings, prices or 2.5%.
- 30 hours’ free childcare from nine months to school; child benefit moved to a household test, tapering from £120k–£160k.
- Business: retain corporation tax rate; maintain/expand full expensing (incl. leasing when affordable); 10‑point SME plan (business rates reliefs, better payment enforcement, access to finance, keep key tax incentives).
- Infrastructure: redeploy £36bn HS2 savings to roads, rail and buses; nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; planning and judicial review reforms to speed delivery.
- Innovation/industry: public R&D to £22bn; AI compute investment; advanced manufacturing plan; support City of London and automotive sector; new trade deals (CPTPP implemented; pursue India, GCC, US when ready).

Work, welfare and skills
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military/cyber year or civic service 25 days).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by curbing “poor‑quality” degrees; Advanced British Standard replaces A‑/T‑level divide; mobile phone bans in schools.
- Welfare reform: tighten PIP and work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes; tougher sanctions; accelerate Universal Credit; new DWP fraud powers.

Borders, security and defence
- Legal, annually falling cap on work/family migration; health checks and higher IHS/insurance where needed; higher salary thresholds sustained.
- Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights; implement Illegal Migration Act; more returns deals; rewrite asylum rules with partners.
- Defence: spend 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn for munitions; faster procurement; 5% of defence budget for R&D; long‑term support for Ukraine.

NHS and social care
- Real‑terms budget rises; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First, 250 GP surgery upgrades/modernisations, 50 more CDCs.
- Tech and productivity plan (£3.4bn): NHS App “single front door,” AI diagnostics, replace outdated IT; cut 5,500 managers.
- Dental recovery plan; women’s health strategy; implement Cass Review; expand mental health support (school teams to 100%, youth hubs nationwide).

Energy, climate and environment
- Net zero 2050 kept with “pragmatic” path: annual North Sea licensing, new gas plants, triple offshore wind, CCUS clusters, SMR fleets and new nuclear (e.g., Wylfa).
- No new green levies or road pricing; protect bills (price cap, standing charge review, Pumpwatch); home efficiency vouchers and £6bn upgrade fund; onshore wind with local consent; protect best farmland from solar; retain fracking moratorium.
- Water: tougher penalties/bonuses bans for polluters; river restoration; reform price reviews; expand tree/peat programmes; new National Park; stronger waste crime action; limit new incinerators.

Housing and communities
- Build 1.6m homes: scrap “nutrient neutrality” barriers with mitigation, fast‑track brownfield in top 20 cities, raise London densities, new development corporations.
- Protect Green Belt; renew Affordable Homes Programme.
- First‑time buyers: permanent SDLT relief to £425k; new Help to Buy; extend Mortgage Guarantee.
- Leasehold reform (cap ground rents, end forfeiture misuse); Renters Reform (abolish Section 21 with court changes); CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- Safer streets: 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentences (violent/sexual/knife crime); four new prisons; victims’ support.
- Drivers: ban pay‑per‑mile; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for 20mph/LTNs; extend £2 bus fare cap; rail reform via Great British Railways.

Society, rights and Union
- Clarify Equality Act: “sex” means biological sex; protect single‑sex spaces and sport; national school guidance on gender questioning.
- Back farmers (farming budget +£1bn, food security target, faster farm infrastructure) and fisheries (renew Seafood Fund, back inshore fleet).
- Strengthen Union: continue direct UK investment in Scotland, Wales, NI; protect internal market; implement Windsor Framework and Troubles legacy body.
